node.statement: Compact realization implies finite complex: for each vertex v of K, let lambda_v be its barycentric coordinate on |K| and U_v={x: lambda_v(x)>0}. The simplexwise affine coordinate formulas agree on common faces, so the weak topology of geometric realization makes each lambda_v continuous and U_v open; every point has a positive barycentric coordinate, so the U_v cover |K|. By the preceding compactness step finitely many U_v cover. Any vertex w not among the selected vertices, viewed as a point of |K|, has lambda_v(w)=0 for every selected v and would be uncovered; hence K has only finitely many vertices. Every simplex is a finite subset of that finite vertex set, so K has only finitely many simplices and is a finite simplicial complex.
